contract_source: sm_federation.wire — the installed distribution, not a copy in this repo
_comment: Every surface the published federation profile defines, with a CLAIM about
whether Orrery implements it. The claim is not a label that exempts: the
suite checks it in BOTH directions.
implemented = true  -> the surface must respond AND validate against the
published schema. A drifted implementation fails.
implemented = false -> the surface must genuinely be absent. The moment it
starts responding, this entry fails and has to be
flipped to true — at which point the schema
validation above applies to it.
So an unimplemented surface cannot be quietly shipped non-conformant, and a
conformant one cannot quietly regress. Nothing is exempted by being listed.
DEPLOYMENT-CONDITIONAL SURFACES. `implemented` is a fact about the RUNTIME.
A surface may additionally depend on what a given DEPLOYMENT can provide —
the §4 feed needs its durable table, so a node with no database, or whose
role cannot create it, degrades to §2-only. Those are different questions and
collapsing them would force a choice between two lies: claiming false for a
surface Orrery implements, or demanding 200 from a node that correctly
refuses to pretend it can serve it.
So such a surface carries `deployment_conditional: true` and the status it
answers when unavailable. The suite then checks the property that actually
matters and is checkable in any deployment: THE ENDPOINT AND THE DESCRIPTOR
AGREE. Serving the feed obliges declaring federation/0.1#4; declaring it
obliges serving it. Nothing is exempted — the unavailable status is pinned,
so a surface cannot go quietly missing behind a 404, and `implemented:false`
still means the route must not exist at all.

surfaces.note: Implemented and merged 2026-08-08. Validated live against the published node-descriptor schema by this suite. Orrery serves §2 only — see the intelligence-feed claim for §4, and the sm-federation protocol notes for why federation_versions cannot say so.

Implemented by the intelligence-feed work; the assertions that judge it landed first. GET /api/federation/intelligence/feed?since=<cursor> serves a signed, hash-chained sm-feed page. server/federation_feed.py backs sm_feed.FeedLog with the durable append-only table public.federation_feed_entries, so the chain outlives the process that wrote it and a reseed is detectable rather than silent. Note precisely what has been demonstrated: server/tests/test_federation_feed.py test_D1 is a STORE-level restart (rebuild from the persisted rows, next append continues at the durable tip). The PROCESS-level assertion is test_feed_restart.py in this directory and it has NOT run — _boot() constructs its TestClient without entering the lifespan, so the instance never runs the boot ensure, never advertises a feed, and always skips, on any deployment. feed_id is the org's did:key — the same key /.well-known/did.json publishes as publicKeyMultibase — so the feed is attributable to the node a peer discovered. The descriptor advertises it as feed_url and build_node_descriptor DERIVES federation/0.1#4 from that, so this claim and the wire declaration cannot disagree. may_degrade: the boot ensure degrades rather than crashing when the app role lacks DDL privilege, when the database is unreachable, or when the DDL file is not in the image — bricking a self-hosted install to add an optional feature is worse than the feature being absent. So an instance that implements §4 may legitimately serve no feed and declare §2 only; presence is not the property to assert, coherence is. Such a node answers 501, not 404: the surface exists in the runtime and this deployment cannot serve it. CORRECTION, previously stated the other way here and in server/constraints.txt: the refusal of sm-bridge's [feed] extra does NOT show Orrery cannot have a completeness-verifiable feed. Two different logs — sm-bridge chains the MEMBER-DELTA store, in-memory and reseeded from a wall-clock base on every restart; the sm-federation feed carries INTELLIGENCE ENVELOPES on a durable store. The refusal stays correct for the delta store and says nothing about this one.

get_our_summary() emits a chapter-shaped document, not a federation-intel/0.1 envelope: no `type`, no `version`, no `generated_at`, and its identity fields are `chapter_id`/`chapter_name` rather than `community_id`/`community_name`. The full field-level delta, with every field classified, is in envelope_field_map.json.

Orrery has a function of the same name with a different contract. The reference returns [{skill, community_id, community_name, weight}] ranked by weight, matching skills exactly. Orrery returns [{our_gap, their_chapter_id, their_chapter_name, their_matching_skills, their_member_count}], unranked, matching by case-insensitive substring in either direction — so `ml` matches `html`. The divergence is in the matching rule, not only the shape, so this is not a rename.
